recent_reviews.review: I thought this lab was a lot more organized than the gen chem lab. There's also not a lab report every week which was very nice. Some of the post lab quizzes were really difficult, but the curve is insanely good. I got a 1/20 on the first quiz and still got an A in the lab overall. She provides lots of resources to succeed and explains things really well.

took CHEM231 with her last semester, and I’m taking CHEM241 with her right now (Spring 2026). my review for that class starts with “Take her!” for reference. there’s a lot of good in this class --- everything I mentioned in my 231 review, in fact. She still brings her love of the game and continues to connect new topics to familiar ones in a way that just works. there’s not much else to add beyond what I wrote there. I’d just recommend making a basic Anki deck for mechanisms on an exam-by-exam basis and continue to review those to stay fresh for synthesis problems. TL;DR: This class is awesome. Dr. Koppel is awesome. Take her class.

take her! there's a lot of good about this class, but I think what stood out to me was her love for the subject that she brought to class every single day (despite all the complaining/lazy/inattentive/grade-grubbing undergrads she had/has to deal with, which i find seriously impressive), be it building a cohesive narrative/thoroughly motivating the various topics we covered as we moved throughout the course, telling stories of past experiment woes, giving real-life context to certain reactions (eg this reaction is regularly used in industry for xyz, if I was doing this in lab I'd probably change this, etc), offering ideas for different ways we could earn a Nobel prize, etc. i think you get the idea. not only were her lectures super engaging, she also just seemed to 'get' how someone new to organic chemistry might struggle (which I did), and taught with that in mind. I've since forgotten what exactly the subject was, but I remember we were discussing a reaction with an unexpected product, and after stepping through one example, she said something along the lines of "let's try xyz, maybe it'll be better [it didn't]". maybe not the most compelling example, but it really resonated with me, as I can't think of many other professors I've had that came with that perspective. Her willingness to abuse notation/skip on some formalism for our understanding also went hard af. other pros: - she provide plenty of resources to help you succeed in the class (as the below reviews have covered, eg the late night show, past exams, creating fresh practice problems to supplement exam prep, etc) - homework is graded on an adjusted scale, with 80% correct being an A - straightforward exams, interesting extra credit problems occasionally. what she covers in lecture is what's tested, there's generally no curveballs, and regrades for TA errors were prompt - good textbook. you get lifetime digital access, it's the same text used in CHEM242, and the text is super straightforward/teaches you what you need to know. would HIGHLY recommend paying the addl $10 for the included practice problems/key. - posts her notes to ELMS as a PDF cons (minor) - lecture not recorded - $30 for Wiley e-text (but wtv, she also offers a FOSS alternative text, it just has a less 1-1 correspondence with lecture topics. reading guide is provided to match though) in summary, 10/10 no notes please do yourself a favor and take her class

Someone even worse than gen chem lab. This has genuinely been the worst lab experience in my life. Everyone has failed the first TAQ and Koppel is very unhelpful. Everything in the lab is broken and my TA tells us to ignore what the manual says every time. The PLQs are also horrible and honestly impossible with knowledge from just what we learn.

Take this professor. I attended GSS weekly and did the practice exams, and I was always well above the average on the exams. Lecture can be a little confusing at times if you don't review the material beforehand, but as long as you keep up with the content, you will be fine. I would definitely recommend taking Koppel! - I thought her exams were fair, and the curve is very generous. She offers Zooms at night with extra practice problems before every midterm and will answer questions. She clearly cares about her students a lot and keeps lecture interesting. Most of these bad reviews are for lab, which was a different story and unavoidable... I still did well in it, but found it to be even harder than lecture. Make sure to go to the TAs with questions, and they can help you out.
She’s a a little intimidating but a really good teacher. I learned a lot and would definitely recommend her!

Review for Lab and Lecture Lecture - Provides past exams that are super helpful, the format and problems on the practice exams were very similar to the actual ones - Very friendly during office hours, takes time to make sure you know the material - Hosts "Late Night Sessions" to do practice problems which is super helpful - The first month was basically gen chem review, stereochem (the first definitive orgo topic) wasnt even on our first exam - Pretty good lecturer, explains things well - Homework was hard at times but all you need is an 80% on all homeworks for Koppel to bump it up to an 100%, and getting an 80% is pretty easy to do, also all homework is due right before an exam, so you can space it out however you want to (which is also nice) General tips (Coming from someone who got an A+ in lecture) - Memorize the flowcharts she gives for the alkene and alkyne reactions - this will make the exams so much easier trust me - try not to miss any lectures, you can get behind very easily and while Koppel does post notes, her handwriting is hard to read and her notes are hard to understand if you did not go to lecture - you dont need to go to discussion (I never did), but you definitely do need to practice outside of class, i mainly went to GSS, office hours, and just studied on my own Lab (I got an A) - Time consuming - The first TAQ was very very hard, I got a 5% (not a typo) on it, however, the next 3 are so much easier, all you need to do is watch the lab video on the ELMS before lab and you can basically ace the TAQs - pre labs were very easy - post labs were at the very least time consuming, and sometimes very hard - my advice is to look up answers, consult friends in lab, go to TA office hours, but also just be willing and ready to accept that some of the problems are incredibly hard to solve - labs themselves were pretty easy, for 2 of the labs, the TA does the lab so you just leave lab after doing the pre lab quiz and the TAQ (if you have one) which takes like 20 minutes - also you do basically all labs with a partner, so it makes it much better Overall comments - in my opinion Koppel is pretty over hated. She provides the resources needed to pass, is a good lecturer, and I really like her Homework policy. Her labs aren't that bad just be prepared to completely fail the first TAQ

If you get stressed easily by professors that have a disorganized way of teaching Dr.Koppel is not the teacher for you. She begins each topic with the general ideas and then focuses in on smaller topics but there are no order or outlines to follow. Looking back over my notes was a nightmare and if you miss a class and look at her posted notes, you will be beyond confused. I highly recommend the Orgo as a second language books if taking this course. The curve is based off of class average which was decently high for my class but I passed with a C with a 58 somehow. The online quizzes and assignments boost your grade but the exams and TLQ in lab are challenging and she does not give you any type of review and will usually be 1/3 of the way through new material, before the exam which gets hard to manage. If you dedicate the time and are good at self-teaching she's not a bad teacher but you cannot slack off or have a bad week you will fall behind orgo is alot of material!

I took this lab in Spring 2025, and I’m not going to lie—this lab is cheeks. It’s definitely better than CHEM132 but worse than CHEM242, so at least the good news is that the grass is greener on the other side. There is simply way too much work for a 1-credit course. Most weeks, you have both a post-lab worksheet and post-lab questions. You lowkey have to go to office hours if you want to do well on the labs. Some weeks are lighter and only require a lab worksheet, but then you’re expected to study for a TAQ, which is basically a quiz on the lab experiment. The TAQs are pretty hard and you need to know not only every step of the lab but also the underlying conceptual theory. My TA was just as confused as we were and was rarely prepared for lab. Most of the time, he would figure things out as we were actively doing the experiment. People often complain that TA office hours are useless, but my advice is to go to another TA's office hours and find one that basically gives out the lab answers. I will say, the lab practical is very easy, and you can probably find the review document or a Quizlet online. The only reason I ended the course with an A is because there’s a very generous curve at the end and my 91% was curved up to an A. Good luck, and honestly, just try your best.
I have never hated a lab more; half the time things didn't work. But she curved my 80 to an A-

horrible ahh 1 credit lab. taq's are IMPOSSIBLE. genuinely no idea what was going on for any of them. average was a 5/20 so im really struggling to understand why they're even administered if everyone fails. i guess it helps if ur in her lecture, but personally i was not and i was taking these quizzes on topics i hadn't even learned yet. the plq's are also really hard some weeks. GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS THEY WILL HELP, but honestly it all depends on which TA is grading them that week, some are nicer and more forgiving than others. the lab itself was fine me and my partner made stuff up half the time and no one cared, as long as u looked like u were busy. curve was really good. i had an 85 raw and it was curved to an a, and i know someone who had a 68 and was rounded to a b-. i have heard shes very unapproachable if u ever have a problem, but my ta was very nice and understanding 99% of the time i asked her anything, but u dont get to pick ur ta so it's really all luck. honestly gl and study for those taq's to the best of ur ability- it will really help separate u from the average grades at the end of the semester

Organic Chemistry is a complicated course, and nothing is going to make it easier. This course is more about understanding than CHEM131. Dr. Koppel has definitely made CHEM231 better after my awful experience with CHEM131. Her homework can be a bit challenging, but it does help with understanding the materials. I recommend doing your homework two weeks before the due dates. Koppel also does some practice problems during the lecture, but don't just rely on those practice problems; definitely go through ELMS and try out other practice problems that she posted, and try her practice exams. Organic Chemistry as a Second Language textbook/PDF is going to help you a lot. She gives generous curves/cut-offs, so that is a plus. Her exams are fair. The averages for midterms are usually around 60% and the final is around 46-55%. Her curves/cut-offs depend on the performance of the whole class, so if you want to do well in this class, definitely study a lot, practice mechanisms (understand how the mechanisms work and why), and ask questions. Try to get a little above the class average, and you will pass the course.

Honestly here is my breakdown that I wish someone would tell me before taking this class: - I don't go to lecture, she's lwk very confusing. I realized her teaching style is just not for me because she goes so so fast. But if u do miss lecture just know the notes she posts are garbage. They're highkey her scribbles from in class. You actually need to attend those lectures. -READ THE TEXTBOOK. this will save you. never went to lecture, just read the textbooks and that CLUTCHED. The last exam I figured the strat was to skip lecture and read the textbook.. I got a 96. take that as u will. -the final exam was slight hard... I think that's why our curve was so good. -she has extra credit points, she gave out 4 this semester and they're usually the day before break. so once before fall break and once before winter break I think. but if u seriously can't make those days u can ask a friend to write ur name down on the attendance sheet because lwk no one checks. Overall: Guys just take koppel. If anything listen to this: my 85 seriously got curved to an A. Like what. All the reviews that are saying not to take her just aren't meant for the course. Because let's be so for real this IS organic chemistry. It's not gonna be easy. But if u study enough you can easily get that A in this class. GOOD LUCK GUYS!!

As a 1 credit course, like the other reviews say, this class is a LOT of work and very disorganized. Oftentimes you will find yourself writing the same things in many different places. But really, it is not horribly difficult, just rather time consuming. Points go as following: 5 points for the pre-lab quiz (pretty straightforward if you read the procedure), 5 points for the notebook pages (pretty straightforward too), 20 points for the worksheets (straightforward as long as you did the experiment or the makeup), and 20 points for either the PLQ (post lab questions) or TAQ (theory and applications quiz)...and no, they are not as notorious as people say. All you need to do for PLQs to do well on them (coming from someone who repeatedly scored 90%+ on them) is to understand the procedure of the lab: not necessarily which chemicals were used, but the objective of the lab. Essentially, they are to apply the objective of the lab to a different set of chemicals, as a sort of "what if" situation. Office hours help A LOT. Sometimes they were very confusing, other times pretty easy. But do not ever wait last minute to do them, that's how you screw up. TAQs are like PLQs, but instead of having a week or two to do it, you have only 10 minutes in class. These...are horrible to say the least. Because they are so rushed, getting a 10/20 or above will feel like luck. Class averages for these being under 5/20 are no exaggeration. Overall, it is possible to do well in the course. You just need to be able to understand the objective of each procedure to pass.
Lab over the summer felt like a fever dream. It was so fast-paced and fried me. My TA also didn't quite seem to know what he was doing! Just come prepared for each lab.

Taking this over the summer probably wasn't the best idea. I grasped the pace of the course while taking it. Orgo requires a lot of memorization, which does not couple well with a short amount of time. Also, a solid foundation of it is key to succeeding in Orgo 2. Professor Koppel is not as bad as I thought. She cares and does her best. However, it's just difficult to sit through 10 hours of lecture consecutively in a week, alongside the lab. Not recommended over the summer!

She’s a nice lady and I don’t think she’s a bad professor. However, I was blindsided about the curve for this class because it is based on the class average after each exam. With that being said, if your class overall did well that semester, the cut off might be higher. The class average for my class was 72% which is relatively high for orgo 1 compared to other orgo 1 classes.

Genuinely one of the worst professors I’ve ever had. Sends emails out SUNDAY nights about what we need to do for lab the next week. I’d say reports are graded more strict than 132. There has been multiple occasions where I go in for office hours and the TAs will tell me my post labs are all correct but when I submit them I get a 10/20. Doesn’t seem like the TAs know how to do it either. I’ve also heard from multiple TAs that Dr koppel tells them to be as strict as possible with grading and give minimal points.

Listen, chem lab will be chem lab, but I enjoyed this lab much more than gen chem. Go to the TAs office hours. My only thing is don't go to office hours without trying to do the work yourself. If you go in with some basic understanding, things will make much more sense and it'll be easier for the TA to help. Also, make sure you know the concepts because you keep building on it throughout the semester. The TAQs can be confusing but they're not as bad as people make them out to be. Not saying that I got 100s, just saying that you can at the very least get above the average if you review the theories. I do agree with others on this course being a lot of work for 1 credit but it's to be expected.

As a 1 credit course, this lab is a lot more work than I believe 1 credit should be offering. Not only is there 3 hour lab once a week, but the post-lab questions, post-lab worksheets, studying for TAQs, and completing pre-labs often takes me 3 hours total to finish. This class took a lot of my time and effort and I think some of the grading rubrics of PLQs are quite strict/too rigid. I think the course was interesting and definitely taught me some new things, but it is overall just way too much work for a 1 credit course. Furthermore, office hours for the TAs were often very unhelpful. I went to many office hours for different TAs and half of them do not know what is going on. They don't know how to answer our post lab questions either and going to multiple TAs will give you different answers that completely vary from each other.

I already wrote a review for her but I realized I left out a very important con of taking her: her notes are actually awful. She basically just scribbles down random structures and then uploads them on canvas so if you miss class you're screwed. She also has really bad handwriting that I have trouble reading even though I have bad handwriting.

As a person, she is very sweet and she cares a lot about her students. As a professor, she can be kind of hard to follow and unorganized. I think this more so had to do with the course and the difficulty of the content. I believe she is probably one of the better options for orgo, but in all honesty we can all agree there really isn't a "good" option in the umd chemistry department.

Who's old, miserable, and unaware? You guessed it, Dr. Koppel!!! She refuses to acknowledge that things need to improve within her course. And coming from a TA the average for the first lab quiz was a 3.7/20.

This class so far has been fine. TAQ 1 was a little challenging, but honestly not crazy (I'd review how to tell the density of diff molecules lol) as long as you had a solid theoretical understanding/intuition for extraction (rtfm!). Given the semester GroupMe was rampant with people asking braindead questions 24/7 (eg what experiment are we doing this week??? what reagents does that need !?!?!1/1///???), I suspect that may be the majority of the 1-star reviews Dr. Koppel received below; that is to say I wouldn't stress too hard abt this class. TL;DR not terrible, just accept this class will be more work than the 1 credit suggests (and know OH are a tremendous help).
Genuinely more disorganized than Chem 132...

You’re going to make the labs go full length most of the time? Fair. You’re gonna make us do the procedure ourselves? Fair. You’re going to thoroughly quiz us on material within the lab book? Fine. You’re going to give us post-lab questions on things we never learned, and there’s no way to know, other than maybe one cruddy, unrelated example from the lab book, which provides maybe a fifth of the information needed to answer the question? I don’t think so. Not a one-credit class. This lab is harder than lecture! I did marginally better on exams from lectures than the plqs/taqs here, while spending less time. It is preposterous and vicious to put people through this!

If you took Friedman, Dr. Koppel will feel like a lifesaver. I nearly failed General Chemistry, but with Dr. Koppel for Organic Chemistry, I got an A. I loved her class. She explains things clearly and gets straight to the point. Honestly, I love her teaching style—though my only comparison is Friedman. She's very straightforward and will tell you exactly what you need to know and what you don’t. For example, if she thinks a topic isn’t worth stressing over (like nomenclature), she won’t overemphasize it. That part was like 10 points on Midterm 1 and never showed up again. She thoroughly explains concepts in a way that makes sense if you’re paying attention. Her exams are fair and similar to the practice problems she gives—she provides lots of practice. If she’s still teaching lab, she connects it to what you’re doing in class, which helps a lot. (side note about lab: go to office hours IT WILL SAVE YOUR GRADE, but find the ones that are actually helpful). A lot of people struggle with mechanisms, but those of us who had Koppel at least understood the basics, especially for lab concepts like radicals. And if you need more help in her class, she provides supplemental videos in the lab that can be used in lecture portions. That’s just my experience, though. Some people feel she goes too fast, but I haven’t heard many complaints about the difficulty of her exams. Honestly, it’s one of those “you either get it or you don’t” situations—but that applies to any professor 😭 Some notes on Professor Koppel and my experience: - I didn’t go to office hours or ask questions in class, but I did sit in the front. - I started studying several days in advance using YouTube videos, one-pagers, practice problems, and flashcards. I didn’t really use the textbook. - The homework setup is a bit unusual — you have until each midterm to complete the corresponding sets. You only need about 80% for full credit. I mostly used the homework to study the week before each exam. - Her exams are very fair. If you do the practice exams, you’ll be well prepared. The final was long but also fair. - For mechanisms, use flashcards and practice them repeatedly. - Go to all the late-night review sessions and practice exams — they help a lot. - She seems funny and nice; she often cracks jokes during class. - My TA was also really helpful in explaining things.

(Fall 2024) Insane workload for a 1-credit lab course. I found I was spending hours on work outside of lab. In my opinion, the lab itself is structured badly and not very well aligned with the 231 course. Lab experience is very dependent on TA. Didier was great at making a 6:30-9:30 lab feel not miserable and having good vibes, even if he wasn't always the most knowledgeable. I never interacted with Koppel herself, but there was an incident where at office hours, multiple TAs didn't understand the post-lab question/what she was looking for, and one went up to ask. She sent him back down with nothing, and told him that he was giving us too much help. Really soured my taste on her. Average weekly workload for the lab looks like: - Pre-Lab Writeup (Objective, Procedure, Reagent Table with structures) - Pre-Lab Worksheet (Mostly fine if you read the theory/procedure, but sometimes confusing) - Watch the lab video (Not always necessary) - Pre-Lab Quiz (A grade boost as long as you read the procedure. A total no-brainer.) - Post-Lab Worksheet (Answering a few questions based on things in lab. Functionally a lab report. Not terrible.) - Post-Lab Questions (Evil. Oftentimes not related to anything done in lab, vaguely about theory. It's hard to understand what she actually wants in an answer. Office hours are a saving grace, but even the TAs don't always know what she wants or how to answer the question. Also, for two different weeks, required reading grad-school level papers.) On the bright side, if you have to take orgo 2 lab, doing this one first will make it feel like a walk in the park!

Take her!!! She teaches in a very organized, easy to follow way, and keeps lecture interesting. As someone who learns from examples, she offers so much practice: test-like example problems in class, worksheets on cavas, late night problem-solving zoom session, and any other type you request if you visit her during office hours. Her exams are very predictable and very fair-- it will never be something you have not seen before. Yes-- all of the orgo professors are good, but when comparing her to the others (who my friends took) her organization of content made more sense to me (and she has a nice curve AND homework to help!). As far as exams, it is very possible to get an A, even above-- there is extra credit! When looking at grades, they seem to be mostly determined by how much you study. The best advice I can give for Koppel is: study content as you get taught it in lecture, go to her late night zooms (test questions directly from!), study in advance so that if you are slightly confused on anything-- office hours!

I did not enjoy this class whatsoever and it is not worth the amount of effort you put in for a 1 credit class. The labs don't always match up with what you're learning in lecture and there isn't much guidance on how to approach questions, definitely go to office hours for extra help. There were also quizzes she'd give you that were horrible, I think one of them had an average of like 8/20 but wasn't curved. The class is curved at the end though and was very generous, as I got an A- from an 84%.
